decisions.reversible: Yes — cost is the instrument's piece. It may change path or shape by editing COST.md §6.1; the renderer follows the file. What would overturn it: a field the transcript cannot honestly produce.
decisions.relayed: Could not SendMessage to the instrument agent (no ListAgents tool in this session; both plausible names unreachable). Relayed through the orchestrator (main), which confirmed delivery.

decisions.ruling: The renderer derives NO dollar figure. Anything the ledger does not state renders as an em dash and is listed under 'problems in the ledger'. Consequence: the instrument must emit ch_pct_of_baseline, usd_per_agent_hour, changes[].delta_pct and every guard status itself.
decisions.reversible: Yes, but reversing it recreates the second implementation rule 10 forbids. The self-test's arm D exists to keep it honest.

decisions.ruling: window.complete must be stated true for the headline to read 'Spend to date'. Absent or false and it reads 'Spend in this window' with an explicit note that earlier spend is not included — because the instrument may have to roll up incrementally as the transcript grows.
decisions.reversible: Yes — one boolean in the contract.

self_test.arms: A fixture with known numbers / B no ledger / C unparseable ledger / D present but PARTIALLY WRONG (numeric string, null, boolean, negative) / E stale 3h / F refresh failed
self_test.controls: arm A's assertions are run against arms B, C and D and must FAIL; arm B's and arm F's are run against A and must FAIL. An assertion set that passes on every arm proves nothing.
self_test.delete_the_fix: Made num() 'helpfully' coerce a numeric string, on a copy of the file. Arm D immediately went red: the page printed a confident $1,234.56 it had not measured. Restored; green again. The instrument can fail.
